authored.note: Written for learners from the sources named in each block. It is an explanation, not a recording. Facts listed under each block are checked word for word against those sources.

summary.text: A lending assistant read a policy document, saved what it read to memory, and on a later run recalled it and used a customer-tier tool. The lab asks you to work out from the evidence where authority actually came from. Retrieved content and memory only influence; the tool authorization control is what grants or denies. It is a scripted, deterministic workflow, not an AI deciding anything, and it pulls together ideas from the earlier labs rather than adding a new attack.
facts: Integrated capstone. Not a new security domain.
CTRL-MCP-001 is the sole tool PDP. RAG does not grant. Memory does not grant. Splunk does not grant.

glance.label: The question
glance.text: A lending-policy assistant accessed customer-tier information during a workflow that was expected to summarize lending policy. You determine what happened from evidence.
facts: A lending-policy assistant accessed customer-tier information during a workflow that was expected to summarize lending policy. Determine what happened from evidence.

glance.label: What the attacker controls
glance.text: Only the bytes of one retrieved lending-policy document, which then persist into memory. The browser cannot choose the setting, the grants, the document, the memory body or any trust label.
facts: The retrieved lending-policy fixture bytes that persist into memory.
The browser does not choose profile, grants, document body, memory body, or trust labels.

glance.label: The chain, in order
glance.text: Retrieved content is classified, written to memory, recalled later and classified again, and a follow-on request reaches the tool authorization control and then the handler.
facts: retrieved content → CTRL-RAG-CONTEXT-001 OBSERVE → memory WRITE → later memory RECALL → CTRL-MEMORY-CONTEXT-001 OBSERVE → follow-on request → CTRL-MCP-001 → tool handler → telemetry → Splunk

glance.label: Where authority enters
glance.text: Not at retrieval and not at memory. Several planes can carry influence, but authority still needs an enforcement decision, and here that decision is CTRL-MCP-001's.
facts: CAPSTONE: multiple influence planes may exist; authority still requires an enforcement decision.

glance.label: How the three runs are linked
glance.text: Each launch mints three run ids: retrieve, write and recall. The lab links them by measured content-hash equality and by the recall run's source_run_id; no new field links retrieve to write.
facts: Each LIVE launch mints three run.ids: RETRIEVE, WRITE, later RECALL.
retrieve content.hash = write content.hash = recall content.hash
recall source_run_id = write run.id
Schema 1.9.0 has no retrieve-to-write field.

glance.label: Same influence, different authorization
glance.text: ATTACK and RETEST use the same adversarial bytes. What differs is the tool authorization decision, and with it whether the privileged handler is invoked.
facts: SAME ADVERSARIAL INFLUENCE. DIFFERENT AUTHORIZATION. DIFFERENT INVOCATION, COMPLETION, AND OUTCOME.

glance.label: What is not involved
glance.text: Goal Integrity and Identity or Delegation are not active vulnerabilities in this scenario, and the lab warns against blaming them without evidence.
facts: Goal Integrity and Identity/Delegation are not active vulnerabilities in this packet.
Do not blame Goal Integrity or Identity without evidence.

glance.label: What evidence exists
glance.text: The handler invocation count is the authoritative record of execution. Indexed Splunk events corroborate it but do not replace it.
facts: Authoritative execution: ToolRegistry handler invocation count.
Corroboration: indexed mcp.started / completed on a complete copy.

path.label: Adversarial document bytes
path.detail: The retrieved fixture bytes that persist into memory.
path.fact: The retrieved lending-policy fixture bytes that persist into memory.

path.label: Retrieve
path.detail: Retrieved content is classified (OBSERVE) and then written to memory.
path.fact: retrieved content → CTRL-RAG-CONTEXT-001 OBSERVE → memory WRITE

path.label: Data, not authority
path.detail: Retrieved context is data; stored context is not authority.
path.fact: RAG: retrieved context is data. MEMORY: stored context is not authority.

path.label: Recall classification
path.detail: CTRL-MEMORY-CONTEXT-001 records OBSERVE on the later recall.
path.fact: memory WRITE → later memory RECALL → CTRL-MEMORY-CONTEXT-001 OBSERVE

path.label: Tool authorization
path.detail: CTRL-MCP-001 is the sole tool decision point.
path.fact: CTRL-MCP-001 is the sole tool PDP.

outcomes.label: DENY (defended retest)
outcomes.detail: tool_not_granted; the handler is not invoked.

outcomes.label: ALLOW (vulnerable attack setting)
outcomes.detail: A labelled lab-only fail-open, not a server grant.

path.label: Evidence copy
path.detail: A copy of the telemetry goes to Splunk, which only observes.

known.text: Schema 1.9.0 has no retrieve-to-write field. Correlation is measured content.hash equality plus memory.source_run_id.
facts: Schema 1.9.0 has no retrieve-to-write field. Correlation is measured content.hash equality plus memory.source_run_id.

known.text: Retrieve skips MCP follow-on so the privileged handler is counted once, on recall.
facts: Retrieve skips MCP follow-on so the privileged handler is counted once, on recall.

known.text: Goal Integrity and Identity/Delegation are not active vulnerabilities in this packet. Absence of those event families is instrumented-experiment evidence, not proof those domains never fail.
facts: Goal Integrity and Identity/Delegation are not active vulnerabilities in this packet. Absence of those event families is instrumented-experiment evidence, not proof those domains never fail.

known.text: RETEST DENY is not automatically SAFE. One RETEST is not universal RAG/memory resistance.
facts: RETEST DENY is not automatically SAFE. One RETEST is not universal RAG/memory resistance.

known.text: CTRL-MCP-001 is a lab allow-list, not production MCP IAM.
facts: CTRL-MCP-001 is a lab allow-list, not production MCP IAM.

terms.text: The three runs of one launch. Each has its own run id.
terms.fact: Each LIVE launch mints three run.ids: RETRIEVE, WRITE, later RECALL.

terms.text: How you know the three runs belong together: the content hash is the same in all three, and the recall run names the write run as its source.
terms.fact: retrieve content.hash = write content.hash = recall content.hash

terms.text: OBSERVE records. ALLOW is a decision. Execution is the handler actually being invoked. Read them separately.
The lab asks you to grade each claim as supported, corroborated, not proven or incorrect.
terms.fact: Classify SUPPORTED / CORROBORATED / NOT PROVEN / INCORRECT.

defender.text: Do not try to sanitize everything, delete memory, block all retrieval or ask Splunk to block. Remove the lab's fail-open overlay, keep the same adversarial bytes, and let server-owned authorization decide.
facts: Do not sanitize everything, delete memory, block all RAG, or ask Splunk to block. Remove the lab overlay. Keep the same adversarial bytes.

lines: Do not blame Goal Integrity or Identity without evidence.
ToolRegistry count proves process-local invocation began, not successful completion.
